reasons.C: Closest in movement: long periodic sentences, parallel openings ('Let us grant... Let us admit') and a semicolon-balanced close, in an earnest arguing stance with the period's diction; the dashes and one rhetorical question are slightly off.
reasons.A: Good balanced sentences and semicolon antithesis with the right period diction, but the parenthetical exclamation and the dash push it towards a playful tone the passage never takes.
reasons.B: Has the semicolon joins and 'I do not say... I say only' stance, but the whimsical asides ('Well:', 'mind you', the bracketed exclamation) and the contraction 'it's' read as caricature and break the period register.
reasons.D: Modern plain-essay voice: short declarative sentences, contemporary diction ('opportunity', 'badge') and a tidy slogan ending, with none of the passage's long balanced periods.
